idea:
Use 4D Gaussian Splatting (4DGS / dynamic 3DGS) as the representation or temporal-consistency backbone for stable, jitter-free 4D hand-object interaction (HOI) reconstruction from video.

Motivating observation (from our own experiments): We ran 4 HOI reconstruction methods on real videos (wild clips + a HOI4D egocentric kettle clip with GT RGB-D) — (1) render_and_compare, the user's own CHOIR-spine per-clip optimization method (MANO hand + model-free object mesh + 6-DoF trajectory + contact); (2) do-as-i-do, a 7-stage pipeline (SAM3 segmentation → SAM-3D object mesh → MoGe/GT pointmaps → HaWoR hands → GeoCalib gravity → TAPIR velocity → guided-diffusion object tracking, ~8.5h/clip); (3) ForeHOI (feed-forward, DepthAnything3 + FoundationPose); (4) HORT (feed-forward point cloud). ALL of them produce temporally jittery / floating hands and objects. Diagnosed root causes: per-frame monocular estimators are independently noisy — HaWoR hand-depth wobble (frame-to-frame depth correlation 0.775, wiggle ratio 7.9), per-frame depth/scale inconsistency, per-frame pose regression with no temporal coupling. Temporal smoothing (median/average filters on trajectories) was only a band-aid. Even with GT depth injected (HOI4D), and even with hours of per-clip optimization or guided diffusion, jitter persists because errors are optimized per-frame or with weak temporal priors.

The user's insight: with the SAME multi-hour per-clip compute budget, a high-quality 4D Gaussian Splatting reconstruction of the dynamic scene can be built that is temporally smooth and stable (photometric consistency across ALL frames jointly enforces temporal coherence). So: can 4DGS be used as the foundation for HOI reconstruction that is stable by construction? Candidate framings to branch on (non-exhaustive, please expand): (a) reconstruct dynamic scene as 4DGS first, then fit/extract MANO hand + rigid object 6-DoF from the coherent Gaussian trajectories (GS as a temporal denoiser/scaffold); (b) template-embedded Gaussians — attach Gaussians to MANO mesh + object mesh and optimize pose/shape parameters directly through GS rendering loss (analysis-by-synthesis with photometric supervision across all frames jointly, like GaussianAvatar/GART-style but for HOI); (c) hybrid: rigid-object Gaussians constrained to SE(3) trajectory + articulated hand Gaussians rigged to MANO, plus contact constraints between them; (d) use 4DGS as pseudo-ground-truth generator / distillation target for training feed-forward HOI models.

Setting constraints: monocular RGB video (egocentric like HOI4D or third-person wild clips), model-free/unknown objects preferred (SAM-3D or GS-native object shape), RGB-D optionally available (HOI4D GT depth). Per-clip optimization time budget of several hours is ACCEPTABLE (already paying it). Hardware: 2× RTX 4090 48GB. The user's existing assets: working MANO fitting (HaWoR), object segmentation (SAM3), object mesh gen (SAM-3D), metric depth (MoGe/DA3-metric), point tracking (TAPIR), the render_and_compare optimization framework, and the HOI4D GT-depth eval harness we just built (kettle clip, depth/size/contact metrics).

Novelty check should cover (2023–2026): existing Gaussian-splatting hand/object works — e.g. hand avatar GS (GaussianHand, 3D Gaussian hand avatars, GART, GaussianAvatar), HOI-specific GS (any "GaussianHOI"-type papers, MANUS grasp capture, hold/HOLD-style neural implicit HOI, BundleSDF, Dyn-HaMR temporal hand), dynamic scene GS (4DGS, Deformable-3DGS, Dynamic 3DGS tracking by persistent Gaussians, Shape-of-Motion, MoSca, SplaTAM), and whether anyone has done contact-aware template-embedded GS for monocular in-the-wild HOI with unknown objects. Key question: is the gap real — stable temporally-coherent 4D HOI from monocular video via GS-based joint optimization — and what is the minimal doable pipeline that beats our current 4 baselines on stability (jitter metrics) while keeping accuracy (we have the HOI4D GT harness to prove it)?

framing.core_idea: Replace per-frame, weakly-coupled monocular estimation in 4D hand-object-interaction (HOI) reconstruction with 4D Gaussian Splatting as the temporal-consistency backbone: since a multi-hour per-clip budget is already being spent, spend it instead on a dynamic-GS reconstruction whose joint multi-frame photometric optimization makes hand (MANO) and unknown-object (SE(3) + model-free mesh) trajectories temporally smooth BY CONSTRUCTION — eliminating the jitter/floating that all 4 tested pipelines (render_and_compare, do-as-i-do, ForeHOI, HORT) exhibit, while matching accuracy on the existing HOI4D GT-depth harness. Candidate instantiations range from GS-as-scaffold (reconstruct then fit templates), template-embedded Gaussians (optimize MANO/object pose through the rendering loss), contact-coupled compositional GS, to GS as pseudo-GT for distilling stable feed-forward models.
framing.user_goal: Identify whether a real, publishable gap exists for stable temporally-coherent monocular 4D HOI reconstruction via GS-based joint optimization (unknown objects, egocentric or wild video), and define the minimal doable pipeline — on 2x RTX 4090 with existing assets (HaWoR, SAM3/SAM-3D, MoGe/DA3, TAPIR, render_and_compare, HOI4D eval harness) — that demonstrably beats the 4 existing baselines on jitter/stability metrics without sacrificing accuracy, targeting a CVPR/ICLR/CoRL/NeurIPS submission.

branch.title: 4DGS-first: dynamic Gaussian reconstruction as a temporal denoiser, then extract MANO + rigid-object SE(3) from persistent Gaussian trajectories
branch.angle: Two-stage decoupling: solve temporal coherence FIRST in a template-free representation (persistent/tracked dynamic Gaussians a la Dynamic 3DGS / Shape-of-Motion / MoSca), THEN fit semantic templates (MANO hand, SAM-3D object mesh, 6-DoF trajectory) to the already-smooth Gaussian motion field. The GS stage is a drop-in replacement for per-frame HaWoR/depth estimators as the source of 3D evidence.
branch.core_hypothesis: Photometric consistency enforced jointly across all frames makes persistent Gaussian trajectories far smoother than per-frame monocular estimates (HaWoR depth wiggle ratio 7.9); fitting MANO/SE(3) to these trajectories (Procrustes/ICP + robust registration, seeded by per-frame estimates) inherits that smoothness by construction, beating trajectory filtering on jitter metrics without losing HOI4D accuracy.
branch.why_distinct: Cleanly sequential (reconstruct-then-parse): no template is inside the GS optimization loop, so it works even when MANO/mesh initialization is bad, and the GS stage is method-agnostic. Contrasts with b2/b3 where templates ARE the GS parameterization, and with b5 where GS refines an existing HOI solution rather than being the primary reconstruction.

clarification.problem_statement: Monocular 4D hand-object-interaction reconstruction — recovering a metric MANO hand trajectory plus an unknown rigid object's shape and SE(3) trajectory from one RGB video — is today assembled from per-frame estimators that are only weakly coupled in time. On a GT-depth HOI4D harness, all four representative pipelines (render_and_compare, do-as-i-do/HaWoR, ForeHOI, HORT) fail temporally because each frame's 3D evidence is independently wrong: HaWoR hand depth traverses ~8x more z-path than the hand actually moves (wiggle ratio 7.9: 0.53 m path vs 0.067 m net), HORT's hand centroid teleports ~1.15 m in z between frames, and monocular object depth is biased -29% to -81%. Two controls show the failure is structural: swapping in a better metric-depth model (DA3) leaves the object's apparent-size swing unchanged (1.75x -> 1.76x), and output-space filtering (median(9)+moving-average(7)) suppresses only the high-frequency flicker (0.018 -> 0.005) while the low-frequency depth swing survives (1.75x -> 1.59x) — smoothing cannot correct biased evidence, only hide its jitter. The problem: within the already-accepted multi-hour offline per-clip budget (do-as-i-do spends ~3 h on a 5 s clip), make temporal coherence a property of the 3D evidence itself — estimated jointly across all frames — while matching per-frame accuracy (hand MPJPE, object size/depth/ADD) on the same harness.
clarification.technical_core:
A two-stage reconstruct-then-parse pipeline in which a band-limited, template-free persistent-Gaussian motion field replaces per-frame estimators as the sole source of 3D evidence, and templates are extracted from it afterwards by robust registration.

Stage 0 (priors, per clip): camera poses (HOI4D-provided; MASt3R-SLAM/MegaSAM in the wild); point-prompted SAM2 hand/object masks (text prompts already shown to lock onto wrong instances); CoTracker3/TAPIR long-range 2D tracks on the foreground; per-frame metric monocular depth (DA3-metric) aligned by a SINGLE per-sequence affine (scale, shift); HaWoR per-frame MANO only as a seed (median beta, one canonical-frame pose).

Stage 1 (temporal denoiser): a MoSca-style persistent dynamic-Gaussian reconstruction of the foreground. Canonical Gaussians (unprojected from masked depth at keyframes) are skinned by dual-quaternion blending to a sparse SE(3) motion scaffold (~100-200 nodes hand group, ~20-50 object group, grouped by lifted masks — still no template). The critical design choice: node trajectories live in a low-rank temporal basis (cubic B-splines, knot spacing 0.25-0.4 s, i.e. a <=4-8 Hz band limit at 30 fps), so frame-rate jitter is UNREPRESENTABLE — smoothness is a property of the parameterization, not a penalty; simultaneously, joint photometric consistency (L1+D-SSIM) of the SAME persistent Gaussians across all frames triangulates absolute depth from ego-motion + in-hand object-rotation parallax, removing the low-frequency depth bias that filtering provably cannot (the residual 1.59x swing). Additional losses: mask rendering, sequence-affine depth prior, 2D-track reprojection (long-range correspondence through occlusion), ARAP/isometry on scaffold edges, and a soft intra-object rigidity term whose residual is kept as a regrasp/articulation diagnostic.

Stage 2 (parse — templates never inside the GS loop): (a) Object SE(3) trajectory: because persistent Gaussians give explicit cross-time correspondence, per-frame pose is a CLOSED-FORM weighted Umeyama/Procrustes (scale fixed to 1) between canonical and frame-t object-Gaussian positions, robustified by IRLS/Huber against mask bleed and non-rigid stragglers — no ICP, no learned matcher, no pose network. Object shape: TSDF-fuse GS depth renders expressed in the recovered object frame (in-hand scanning for free), optionally registering a SAM-3D mesh once for a CAD-like output. (b) Hand: fit MANO once in the canonical frame (HaWoR seed), bind each hand Gaussian to its nearest MANO surface point (barycentric + LBS weights), then solve theta(t) and root SE(3)(t) per frame by Levenberg-Marquardt on Huber point-to-correspondence residuals with only a weak pose prior and NO temporal smoothness term — the headline ablation shows adding one changes nothing because the evidence is already band-limited, whereas per-frame baselines need filtering and still keep their low-frequency bias. Metric scale is resolved once per sequence via the depth affine plus a canonical hand-size prior on beta (~0.19 m — the same fix that recovered render_and_compare's 0.77x hand). (c) Contact polish: contacts detected from the stage-1 motion field itself (sustained proximity + near-zero relative tangential velocity between hand Gaussians and object surface), then a short joint refinement with contact attraction, MANO-vs-object-SDF non-penetration, and grasp-preserving coupled updates (hand and object moved by the same delta).

Evaluation: HOI4D rigid categories with GT align_depth + GT object pose + MANO GT — accuracy (hand MPJPE/MRRPE, object CD/ADD-S, size/depth error) AND temporal metrics (wiggle ratio, acceleration error, apparent-size flicker and swing, contact stability, penetration), against the four pipelines raw and with ORACLE-TUNED filters (OneEuro/median+MA/spline/Kalman) — the decisive control — plus template-in-the-loop GS/implicit comparators (BIGS, HOLD) and DexYCB/HO3D for cross-paper comparability.
clarification.novelty_claim: First reconstruct-then-parse pipeline for monocular 4D HOI in which a template-free, band-limited persistent-Gaussian motion field is the sole 3D evidence and MANO + object SE(3) trajectories are extracted afterwards by registration against its time-correspondent trajectories (closed-form per-frame Procrustes for the object, skinning-bound trajectory IK for the hand) — making temporal coherence a property of the evidence rather than of output filtering (shown to fix only the high-frequency band: flicker 0.018->0.005 but swing stuck at 1.59x) or of template-in-the-loop rendering losses (BIGS, DyTact, HOLD, Interaction-Aware 4DGS), and contributing the first temporal-coherence benchmark for HOI on HOI4D GT depth with oracle-filtered per-frame baselines as the control.
clarification.target_venue: CVPR (2027, deadline ~Nov 2026) — a 3D-reconstruction systems + analysis paper with a strong empirical harness; no learned component is central (rules out ICLR) and no robot deployment (rules out CoRL); fallback ICCV/3DV.
key_assumptions: Parallax sufficiency: egocentric camera motion plus in-hand object rotation give enough effective baseline for joint photometric consistency to anchor absolute depth better than any per-frame metric-depth prior; on low-parallax segments the method must degrade gracefully to sequence-affine-aligned depth-prior quality rather than diverge.

Monocular dynamic-GS optimization (MoSca / Shape-of-Motion class) converges on egocentric HOI clips despite hand texture-poverty, motion blur, and mutual hand-object occlusion, provided masks, long-range 2D tracks, and depth priors; scaffold persistence carries occluded Gaussians well enough that per-frame registration has usable support on both sides of every occlusion.

Smoothness transfer: because cross-time correspondence is persistent by construction (no per-frame re-matching), Procrustes/IK against band-limited trajectories yields band-limited template parameters — no correspondence flicker at contact boundaries; this is the load-bearing mechanism behind 'smooth by construction' and must hold empirically.

Band-limit validity: 0.25-0.4 s spline knots (<=4-8 Hz) sit above genuine HOI4D manipulation dynamics but below the jitter band (HaWoR wiggle at frame rate); if real motion has faster components the basis clips them (tunable, but a bias-variance knob that must be reported).

Object rigidity within the clip (scope: HOI4D rigid categories — kettle, bottle, mug, toy car); regrasps and articulated objects are detected via the non-rigid Procrustes residual but explicitly out of scope to reconstruct.
Camera poses are available or recoverable: HOI4D provides them; in-the-wild results assume egocentric SLAM (MASt3R-SLAM / MegaSAM) succeeds on handheld HOI clips.

Segmentation lift is reliable: point-prompted SAM2 masks (text prompts already shown to grab the wrong instance on HOI4D) group Gaussians into hand/object well enough that IRLS absorbs residual mask bleed.

Seeding is cheap: one decent HaWoR frame (median beta + canonical pose) suffices to initialize the MANO binding, and metric scale is resolvable once per sequence from the depth affine plus the ~0.19 m canonical hand-size prior that already fixed render_and_compare's 0.77x hand.

Compute budget: multi-hour offline per-clip optimization is acceptable — already the operating point (do-as-i-do ~3 h per 5 s clip on the same harness), with the GS stage estimated at 1-2 h/clip on a single modern GPU.

closest_works.title: Grasp in Gaussians (GraG): Fast Monocular Reconstruction of Dynamic Hand-Object Interactions
closest_works.relation: Closest neighbor and the biggest threat to the framing. Template-free-ish object: SAM3D-initialized dense Gaussians subsampled into a compact Sum-of-Gaussians whose canonical shape is frozen, then per-frame rigid SE(3)+scale tracked with SoG image-alignment, silhouette, depth, contact, and explicit temporal-smoothness losses (acceleration penalties on translation/rotation). Hand is NOT parsed from Gaussians — it refines a per-frame Dyn-HaMR MANO trajectory with 2D-joint + depth losses. Already claims 'temporally coherent' HOI, reports ACC(hand/object), MRRPE, contact/motion deviation on HO3Dv3 + HOT3D, ~36 min/100 frames. Overlaps: Gaussians as the object-pose evidence, temporal-stability headline, closed-form-ish rigid tracking. Differs: smoothness is a penalty during per-frame tracking, not a band-limited parameterization of a jointly-optimized photometric 4D reconstruction; hand never bound to Gaussian trajectories; no HOI4D GT-depth harness, no oracle-filter control, no low-frequency depth-bias analysis.

closest_works.title: Interaction-Aware 4D Gaussian Splatting for Dynamic Hand-Object Interaction Reconstruction
closest_works.relation: Template-free (no object priors) 4DGS for HOI scenes with interaction-aware hand-object Gaussians, evaluated on HOI4D and HO3D — occupies the 'dynamic GS on HOI4D' square. But it is a dynamic-scene reconstruction / novel-view paper: it outputs geometry+appearance, does not extract MANO parameters or an object SE(3) trajectory, and has no temporal-jitter benchmark against per-frame estimator pipelines. It is the branch's natural Stage-1 comparator, not a reconstruct-then-parse system.

closest_works.title: Dyn-HaMR: Recovering 4D Interacting Hand Motion from a Dynamic Camera
closest_works.relation: World-frame hand-only trajectory optimization from moving cameras with motion priors — the strongest existing answer to HaWoR's depth wiggle for the hand half. The branch must beat trajectory-prior smoothing (not just raw HaWoR + filters) to show Gaussian evidence is the better denoiser; GraG already uses Dyn-HaMR as its hand source.

novelty.delta: No published work makes a template-free, band-limited (spline-basis motion-scaffold) persistent-Gaussian reconstruction the SOLE 3D evidence and then extracts semantic templates from it post-hoc — closed-form per-frame Umeyama/Procrustes on persistent object-Gaussian correspondences plus skinning-bound MANO trajectory IK with no temporal smoothness term. Existing Gaussian HOI systems either put templates inside the optimization (BIGS, HOLD, DyTact, MANUS) or track a frozen Gaussian shape per-frame with explicit temporal-smoothness PENALTIES (GraG) — i.e., smoothness as regularization on outputs, whereas this branch makes frame-rate jitter unrepresentable in the evidence itself and claims smoothness transfers to templates by construction. The second genuinely open contribution is the evaluation: a temporal-coherence benchmark on HOI4D GT depth with ORACLE-TUNED output filters on four per-frame pipelines as the control, plus the high-frequency-flicker vs low-frequency-depth-bias decomposition (filtering fixes 0.018->0.005 flicker but not the 1.59x swing) — no found paper isolates that distinction. Caveats to the claim: GraG (Apr 2026) already owns 'temporally stable, template-light Gaussian HOI tracking with acceleration metrics' and is 6.4x faster than HOLD, so the 'first temporally coherent Gaussian HOI' framing is dead — the paper must be positioned as evidence-side band-limiting + reconstruct-then-parse vs GraG's track-with-penalties, and must ablate against a smoothness-penalty variant; Interaction-Aware 4DGS already does template-free 4DGS on HOI4D (but stops before parsing); MoSca supplies Stage 1 nearly wholesale, so novelty rests on the parsing stage, the band-limit argument, and the benchmark rather than the reconstruction machinery.
novelty.crowdedness_reason: Monocular per-clip HOI reconstruction is one of the fastest-moving corners of 3D vision: HOLD (CVPR24), DyTact, BIGS (CVPR25), Interaction-Aware 4DGS (11/25), GraG (04/26), CHOIR (05/26), THO (03/26), plus feed-forward lines (HORT, ForeHOI) and hand-trajectory lines (Dyn-HaMR, HaWoR) — several explicitly claiming temporal coherence with acceleration-error metrics in the last 8 months. The specific reconstruct-then-parse cell (template-free GS evidence -> post-hoc template registration) and the oracle-filter temporal benchmark are still unoccupied, but concurrent-work risk before a Nov 2026 CVPR deadline is high — GraG and CHOIR appeared within the last 3 months alone.

failure_modes: Core mechanism may be theoretically hollow: for a DYNAMIC foreground object, monocular photometric consistency cannot triangulate absolute depth — a rigid moving object has an irreducible size/depth/translation ambiguity under a moving monocular camera (scaling object size and its z-trajectory together re-explains all images). Ego-motion parallax anchors only the STATIC background; in-hand rotation parallax recovers object SHAPE up to scale, not distance. So Stage 1 will make apparent size CONSISTENT nearly by construction (frozen canonical Gaussians => the 1.75x swing metric collapses trivially) while the absolute depth trajectory stays anchored to the same biased DA3 prior (-29% to -81%) via the sequence affine. Result: temporal metrics improve, ADD/depth-error does not, and reviewers correctly read the headline 'removes the bias filtering cannot' as unsupported — consistency was achieved, correctness was not.

The killer ablation the proposal does not include may nullify the entire Gaussian stage: fit the SAME cubic-B-spline band-limited basis directly to template parameters (MANO theta/root + object SE(3)) with the same photometric/mask/track/depth losses — i.e., band-limited template-space bundle adjustment (essentially HOLD/BIGS with a spline basis, seeded exactly as proposed with HaWoR + SAM-3D). If that simpler baseline matches on jitter AND accuracy, the reconstruct-then-parse architecture is unnecessary machinery and the paper's central claim ('evidence-side band-limiting, templates outside the loop') reduces to a parameterization trick that works equally well template-in-the-loop. An AC will demand this ablation and it is genuinely likely to tie.

The band-limited-basis vs smoothness-penalty distinction (the delta against GraG) may be empirically indistinguishable: a well-tuned acceleration penalty realizes the same low-pass transfer function as spline knots. The required ablation (spline basis vs penalty variant, same losses) plausibly shows no significant difference, collapsing the main framing against the closest prior work to 'we chose a different regularizer.'

MoSca/Shape-of-Motion-class optimization is brittle on exactly this footage: texture-poor fast-moving hands, motion blur, fingers self-occluding, object >50% occluded by the grasp. CoTracker3 tracks break at blur/occlusion; 20-50 scaffold nodes on a mostly-hidden object are under-constrained; DQB skinning tears at the hand-object boundary. Expect a meaningful per-clip failure rate (divergence or mush) that forces either cherry-picking (reviewers punish) or honest success-rate reporting that undercuts the 'drop-in replacement for per-frame estimators' claim. MoSca also needs per-scene hyperparameter babysitting, contradicting 'method-agnostic.'

Smoothness-transfer breaks precisely where it matters: at contact/occlusion boundaries the registration SUPPORT SET churns (mask bleed flips boundary Gaussians between hand and object groups, occluded Gaussians drop in/out of IRLS inliers), reinjecting frame-rate jitter into Procrustes/IK outputs even though individual trajectories are band-limited. The headline 'no temporal smoothness term needed' ablation can fail exactly at contact events — the frames the HOI community cares about.

Hand accuracy may regress: MANO IK driven only by 3D Gaussian-correspondence residuals discards image-space keypoint evidence; a single canonical-frame binding (one HaWoR pose, median beta) propagates any canonical-frame error globally; and the 4-8 Hz band limit clips genuine fast finger articulation during grasp establishment/regrasp. Plausible outcome: wins on wiggle/acceleration, loses on MPJPE vs Dyn-HaMR/filtered HaWoR — read as a smoothness-accuracy tradeoff, not a win.

Crowding/scoop risk is acute: GraG (04/2026) already owns 'temporally stable template-light Gaussian HOI tracking' with acceleration metrics at 36 min/100 frames; CHOIR (05/2026) owns 'temporally consistent 4D HOI via multi-stage per-clip optimization'; Interaction-Aware 4DGS already does template-free 4DGS on HOI4D. Another 4-5 months of concurrent work land before the Nov 2026 deadline. The surviving delta (parse-after vs track-with-penalties + oracle-filter benchmark) is a framing-level contribution reviewers can dismiss as 'MoSca + Umeyama + MANO IK — a combination of known components.'

Benchmark contribution is weaker than claimed: THO and GraG already report acceleration/temporal metrics for HOI, so 'first temporal-coherence benchmark' is dead as stated; what remains is the oracle-filter control and the flicker-vs-swing frequency decomposition — a strong ANALYSIS section but not a standalone contribution that carries a CVPR paper, and it is built on HOI4D GT (align_depth holes at hand boundaries, known-noisy object pose annotations) which invites disputes about whether measured 'jitter' partly lives in the GT.

Systems integration burden vs timeline: SAM2 + CoTracker3 + DA3 + MoSca-variant + Procrustes/IRLS + MANO IK + TSDF fusion + contact refinement, then 4 per-frame baselines with oracle filter sweeps, plus HOLD (~10.5 h/clip) and BIGS reproduction, plus DexYCB/HO3D for comparability — at 1-2+ h/clip over the dozens of clips needed for a credible benchmark, this is multi-GPU-weeks of compute and months of brittle glue engineering with ~4.5 months to the deadline.

Scope narrowness: rigid HOI4D categories only, regrasps/articulation explicitly out of scope, single-hand implicitly assumed; GraG evaluates HO3Dv3+HOT3D and handles the same setting faster — reviewers will ask why the 3-hour offline pipeline is worth it when the fast concurrent method exists and the accuracy delta is unproven.
unsound_assumptions: 'Parallax sufficiency' as stated is unsound, not merely risky: joint photometric consistency over a moving monocular camera constrains a dynamic rigid object's depth only up to the size/depth/motion ambiguity; the claimed mechanism for removing the low-frequency 1.59x residual swing (triangulation from ego-motion + in-hand rotation) does not exist for the dynamic foreground. The honest version — 'we enforce consistency and inherit absolute scale from the depth affine + hand-size prior' — is a much weaker claim and must replace the current one.

'Smoothness transfer by construction' assumes a temporally stable registration support set; occlusion- and mask-bleed-driven inlier churn at contact boundaries violates it exactly where evaluation focuses. It is an empirical hope, not a construction.

'Band-limit validity' assumes genuine HOI4D manipulation dynamics live below 4-8 Hz; contact transients and grasp-establishment finger motion plausibly do not, and the assumption is being used to justify removing the very evaluation frames where per-frame methods fail worst.

'Seeding is cheap' (one canonical HaWoR frame + median beta) is fragile: canonical-frame selection is itself a failure point, and errors in that single binding propagate to every frame with no image-space correction path in the proposed IK.

'The GS stage is a drop-in, method-agnostic replacement' contradicts the known per-scene fragility and tuning burden of MoSca-class optimization on adversarial footage (blur, texture-poor skin, heavy mutual occlusion).

Implicit assumption that matching per-frame accuracy while winning temporal metrics clears the CVPR bar in 2026: with GraG/CHOIR/THO all claiming temporal coherence, reviewers will likely require an accuracy win or a decisive mechanism ablation, not parity plus smoothness.

Implicit assumption that the Gaussian intermediate is necessary at all — untested against band-limited template-space joint optimization with identical losses and seeds (the most dangerous missing baseline in the plan).

feasibility.data: Good. HOI4D with GT align_depth, object pose, and MANO is in hand and the eval harness plus four baseline pipelines already run (compare/hoi4d exists in-repo); no new capture needed. Gaps: HO3D/DexYCB runs needed for cross-paper comparability (GraG reports on HO3Dv3/HOT3D), HOI4D GT noise (depth holes at hand boundaries, imperfect object poses) threatens the credibility of fine-grained jitter metrics, and rigid-category filtering shrinks the clip pool.
feasibility.compute: Marginal on the stated setup. 1-2 h/clip (optimistic for MoSca-class + parse + contact refinement) x ~50-100 clips x (method + ~6 ablations incl. spline-vs-penalty and template-space-BA) + oracle filter sweeps on 4 baselines + HOLD at ~10.5 h/clip is multi-GPU-weeks; doable with a small cluster or sustained vast.ai spend, painful on one GPU. The real cost is engineering time: 6+ brittle third-party components integrated in ~4.5 months to the Nov 2026 deadline.
feasibility.evaluation: Strongest asset and biggest trap. The oracle-tuned-filter control and flicker-vs-swing frequency decomposition are genuinely good experimental design and already partially executed. But the decisive tests cut both ways: (1) does Stage 1 actually reduce ABSOLUTE object depth error vs sequence-affine-aligned DA3, or only variance around the same bias — measurable on GT depth in week one; (2) does band-limited template-space optimization without Gaussians tie the full pipeline. If either goes the wrong way the paper's core claim dies, so evaluation is feasible but has high self-refutation risk. Per-clip success rates must be reported to preempt cherry-picking accusations.

pressure.verdict_reason: The problem analysis (filtering fixes high-frequency flicker but not low-frequency depth bias) is genuinely strong and grounded in the user's own harness, and the reconstruct-then-parse cell is technically unoccupied. But the branch has one likely-fatal technical flaw — monocular photometric consistency cannot fix absolute depth bias for a dynamic object, so the mechanism advertised as the cure for the 1.59x residual swing does not exist in principle, only consistency does — and one likely-fatal strategic flaw: GraG/CHOIR/THO have crowded the temporal-coherence-for-HOI claim in the last 8 months, leaving a delta (basis vs penalty, parse-after vs track-with) that a plausible ablation shows is a wash. Do not commit to the full build. Run a 2-3 week kill-test first: (a) MoSca-class Stage 1 on 3-5 HOI4D clips — measure absolute object depth error and swing vs sequence-affine DA3 on GT depth; (b) band-limited template-space joint optimization (same losses, no Gaussians) as the null hypothesis. Pursue only if (a) shows a real absolute-depth win and (b) loses to the Gaussian pipeline; otherwise pivot the paper toward the analysis/benchmark contribution or drop the branch.

digest.kill_test: 2-3 weeks: run MoSca-class Stage 1 on 3-5 HOI4D clips. Go only if absolute object-depth error beats sequence-affine DA3 on GT depth AND band-limited template-space optimization (no Gaussians) loses; else pivot to benchmark paper.

branch.title: Template-embedded HOI Gaussians: MANO-rigged hand Gaussians + mesh-anchored object Gaussians optimized end-to-end through the rendering loss
branch.angle: Analysis-by-synthesis where the ONLY free variables are MANO pose/shape/global trajectory, object 6-DoF trajectory, and Gaussian appearance attached to the templates — a GART/GaussianAvatar-style rig extended to two interacting entities with unknown object geometry (Gaussians initialized on the SAM-3D mesh, optionally refining it). Photometric loss across ALL frames jointly + trajectory smoothness priors replace per-frame keypoint/depth losses.
branch.core_hypothesis: Backpropagating a multi-frame differentiable-splatting photometric loss into low-dimensional template parameters is a fundamentally stronger temporal coupling than any post-hoc filter or per-frame render-and-compare: jitter cannot exist unless it improves photometric fit in every frame, so the solution is stable by construction while pixel-accurate.
branch.why_distinct: Templates are the parameterization inside the GS loop (low-DOF, semantically constrained), versus b1 where GS is free-form and templates come after. This is the direct 'GaussianAvatar-for-HOI' framing and the branch whose novelty hinges most on whether hand-avatar-GS papers already cover interaction with unknown objects.

clarification.problem_statement: Given a monocular (optionally egocentric, moving-camera) RGB(-D) video of a hand manipulating an unknown rigid object, recover a metric, world-frame, temporally consistent 4D reconstruction — MANO shape + pose trajectory, object geometry, and object SE(3) trajectory — under an offline per-clip compute budget. Every existing pipeline, whether feed-forward (HORT, ForeHOI), render-and-compare, diffusion-guided (do-as-i-do), or Gaussian-splatting-based (BIGS CVPR'25, GHOST'26, Grasp-in-Gaussians'26), ultimately keeps PER-FRAME pose variables that are at best weakly coupled by smoothness losses or post-hoc filters; empirically (our HOI4D GT-depth harness) this yields object size errors of +33–43%, absolute depth errors of −29% to −81% for monocular methods, and frame-to-frame jitter/floating of the grasped object in all four tested pipelines — artifacts a filter cannot fix because it never sees pixels. The problem: re-spend the already-accepted multi-hour budget on ONE joint spatio-temporal optimization in which temporal coherence and hand-object attachment are structural properties of the parameterization, while matching or beating per-frame accuracy on metric world-frame benchmarks.
clarification.technical_core: Analysis-by-synthesis over the WHOLE clip where the only geometric unknowns are low-DoF template trajectories, and time-invariant Gaussian appearance rigged to the templates turns texture into a self-supervised tracker (any jitter misaligns the shared texture in every frame and raises the loss). (1) STATE: hand = shared MANO beta + per-joint rotation trajectories as cumulative B-splines (knots at 4–8 Hz) + wrist se(3) spline; N_h Gaussians bound to MANO faces (barycentric anchor + normal offset, LBS-skinned, GART-style pose-corrective blendshapes). Object = canonical SAM-3D mesh (from the best-visibility frame; global scale is a free variable) with face-anchored Gaussians (bounded local offsets) + optional per-vertex displacement field with Laplacian/ARAP regularization to correct SAM-3D's aspect-ratio bias (measured −21% on our kettle clip). (2) CONTACT-FACTORIZED OBJECT TRAJECTORY — the key mechanism: contact segments are seeded from SAM2 mask adjacency + init proximity; during a held segment k, T_obj(t) := T_wrist(t) ∘ G_k with a SINGLE latent grasp transform G_k per segment plus a heavily-regularized slow drift spline for in-hand adjustment; during free segments T_obj(t) is a cumulative se(3) B-spline (continuous-time-SLAM parameterization imported into HOI); segment boundaries get optimizable soft blending. Hand-relative jitter and 'floating' are thus impossible by construction during grasp — not penalized, unrepresentable. (3) LOSSES, summed over frame minibatches spanning the clip: composited depth-sorted rasterization of both Gaussian sets → masked L1 + D-SSIM photometric with per-frame affine exposure; per-entity silhouette vs SAM2 alpha; DINOv2 feature-metric loss for specular/textureless robustness; depth term (GT depth on HOI4D, metric-mono depth in the wild) resolving absolute scale/depth; robust low-weight 2D keypoint anchor (Geman-McClure so per-frame detector jitter is not re-imported); SDF penetration hinge + fingertip attraction during held phases; small acceleration penalties on spline knots. (4) SCHEDULE (~1–4 GPU-h per clip, i.e. do-as-i-do's budget): Stage A — init from HaWoR (world hand + camera) and the existing render_and_compare framework (per-frame object poses via its mask/depth losses), least-squares spline fit, freeze poses, fit appearance; Stage B — joint optimization of splines + grasp transforms + scale, coarse-to-fine in image resolution and knot density (2→8 Hz); Stage C — unlock displacement field and a bounded per-frame residual (±1σ around the spline) to recover true high-frequency motion, reported with/without. (5) EVALUATION on the extended HOI4D GT-depth harness (~20–30 clips): metric size/depth error, world MPJPE, chamfer/ADD vs GT-depth-unprojected reference, plus NEW temporal metrics — acceleration error (mm/s²), pose jitter (deg/frame², mm/frame²), apparent-scale constancy, contact persistence — against the 4 harness pipelines, BIGS, GHOST, and critically against each baseline + OneEuro/SmoothNet/spline post-filtering, the ablation that proves joint pixel-level optimization strictly dominates filtering (filters trade jitter for lag and cannot correct scale/depth/floating).
clarification.novelty_claim: To our knowledge the first HOI reconstruction in which both interacting entities' motions are optimized as contact-factorized continuous-time trajectories (object pose expressed relative to the hand through a per-grasp latent transform, se(3) splines when free) inside a jointly-rendered template-rigged Gaussian-splatting objective — making temporal smoothness and grasp rigidity properties of the parameterization rather than of losses or filters, unlike BIGS/GHOST/Grasp-in-Gaussians which all retain per-frame pose variables — and the first to benchmark GS-based HOI on metric world-frame temporal-stability metrics (jitter, scale constancy, contact persistence) with a GT-depth harness.
clarification.target_venue: CVPR (primary; BIGS/GHOST lineage venue — a systems+evaluation 3D reconstruction paper fits CVPR better than ICLR/CoRL; ICCV/3DV as fallback)
key_assumptions: Object is rigid: SE(3) trajectory + small displacement-field refinement suffices; articulated/deformable objects are out of scope (stated limitation, future work).

SAM-3D produces a topologically usable canonical mesh from at least one high-visibility frame, with errors correctable by the displacement field + silhouette losses (harness evidence: kettle mesh usable but −21% size / aspect-ratio bias).

Per-frame initializations (HaWoR hand+camera, render_and_compare object poses) land within the photometric basin of convergence (~15° / ~3 cm); coarse-to-fine rendering and the DINOv2 feature-metric loss are assumed to widen this basin enough on real clips.

SAM2 video segmentation with point prompts is reliable per entity (the harness already showed text prompts fail with distractor objects and point+negative prompts fix it), and mask adjacency is a good enough seed for contact-segment detection.

Camera intrinsics and extrinsics are available (HOI4D GT; SLAM/HaWoR in the wild) — world-frame smoothness and metric claims degrade with camera-pose error; optional camera-refinement spline mitigates but does not remove this dependency.

Absolute metric scale/depth requires SOME depth signal (HOI4D GT depth for the benchmark, metric monocular depth in the wild) or the hand-size prior; RGB-only operation works but with weaker metric claims.

Object appearance is approximately time-invariant over a clip (per-frame affine exposure absorbs lighting drift); heavy motion blur and strong specularity are handled by loss downweighting, not modeled.

Grasp rigidity holds within detected contact segments up to slow drift (regrasping/rolling manipulation is captured by segment splitting + the drift spline; rapid dexterous regrasps may violate this).
Offline budget of ~1–4 GPU-hours per clip is acceptable (matches the already-spent do-as-i-do budget); this is not a real-time method and does not claim to be.

Enough per-entity visual signal (texture, silhouette motion, or depth) exists to disambiguate pose; textureless rotationally-symmetric objects fall back on silhouette+depth+contact terms with expectedly weaker rotation accuracy (report symmetry-aware metrics).

HOI4D provides sufficient clips with GT depth + object annotations across categories (~20–30 clips) to make the extended harness statistically meaningful, and BIGS/GHOST code runs on it for direct comparison (both repos are public).

closest_works.title: BIGS: Bimanual Category-agnostic Interaction Reconstruction from Monocular Videos via 3D Gaussian Splatting

However, hand and object poses remain per-frame variables coupled only by losses — no continuous-time trajectories, no hand-relative object parameterization, no temporal-stability metrics. This is the paper that removes 'first template-rigged GS for HOI with unknown objects' from the claimable novelty.

closest_works.title: Get a Grip: Reconstructing Hand-Object Stable Grasps in Egocentric Videos
closest_works.relation: Closest precedent for the branch's key mechanism: during a stable grasp it parameterizes object pose RELATIVE to the hand (single base transform + 1-DoF latent-axis rotation) and jointly optimizes across all frames of the grasp — structurally very similar to the per-segment latent grasp transform G_k + drift. Critical differences: requires category CAD templates (not unknown SAM-3D objects), mask+physics losses only (no photometric Gaussian texture-tracking), handles ONLY manually annotated stable-grasp segments (no free-motion splines, no full-clip trajectory), no metric world-frame or jitter evaluation.

closest_works.title: Grasp in Gaussians (GraG): Fast Monocular Reconstruction of Dynamic Hand-Object Interactions

But poses are optimized PER-FRAME in short windows with acceleration-smoothness losses and contact handled as a proximity loss — exactly the loss-based (not parameterization-based) coupling this branch argues against. Reports hand-relative Chamfer but no acceleration/jitter/scale-constancy metrics vs GT depth.

novelty.delta: The generic framing ('MANO-rigged hand Gaussians + unknown-object Gaussians optimized end-to-end through a rendering loss') is ALREADY published — BIGS (CVPR'25) and GHOST/GraG (2026 preprints) do exactly that, so the branch cannot be sold as 'GaussianAvatar-for-HOI'. What no found work does is the branch's actual technical core: (1) making the ENTIRE clip's geometric state continuous-time and contact-factorized — object pose defined as T_wrist(t) ∘ G_k (one latent grasp transform per contact segment + regularized drift) during grasps and a cumulative se(3) B-spline when free — so hand-relative jitter and floating are unrepresentable rather than penalized, inside a jointly rendered two-entity Gaussian objective with unknown object geometry. Get a Grip (ECCV'24) has the hand-relative grasp constraint but only for CAD-template objects, mask-only losses, and isolated pre-annotated grasp segments; HOIGS has splines-in-GS but for full-body scenes with world-frame object poses; SplineGS-family shows splines are a commodity component. (2) No GS-based HOI work benchmarks metric world-frame temporal stability (acceleration error, pose jitter, apparent-scale constancy, contact persistence) against GT depth, nor runs the 'baseline + OneEuro/SmoothNet post-filter' ablation the branch proposes as its central evidence. The novelty is therefore real but narrow and mechanism-level: parameterization-as-constraint (contact factorization + continuous time) plus a temporal-stability evaluation protocol, and the paper must be written and ablated around exactly that delta against BIGS/GHOST/GraG, not around the rigged-Gaussians framing.
novelty.crowdedness_reason: Category-agnostic HOI reconstruction from monocular video is a fast-moving lineage with multiple papers per cycle (HOLD CVPR'24, Get a Grip ECCV'24, G-HOP CVPR'24, BIGS CVPR'25, Hand-held Object Reconstruction CVPR'25, GHOST, Grasp-in-Gaussians, ManiSplat, HOIGS all in the 2026 preprint wave), and the Gaussian-splatting instantiation specifically has at least four 2025-26 entries. GraG already claims temporal stability as its headline benefit, so the window for the 'per-frame poses are the problem' pitch is actively closing; however, the specific contact-factorized continuous-time parameterization and the temporal-stability benchmark are unclaimed, so it is crowded rather than saturated.

failure_modes: Core hypothesis can backfire empirically: T_obj(t) := T_wrist(t) ∘ G_k hard-wires HaWoR wrist-tracking error (jitter, drift, depth bias — worst exactly when the hand is occluded by the grasped object) directly into the object trajectory. If mask/depth-based object evidence is locally better than wrist tracking, the factorization DEGRADES object accuracy versus per-frame baselines, and the headline 'parameterization dominates losses' claim collapses. The escape hatches (drift spline, soft segment blending, Stage-C bounded per-frame residuals) each reintroduce the per-frame DOF the pitch says are unrepresentable — a sharp reviewer will call the final system 'per-frame poses with a strong spline prior', i.e., exactly the loss/filter coupling the paper attacks.

The photometric-tracker premise is weakest where jitter is worst: during manipulation the object is 50–80% hand-occluded, hands are near-textureless and self-similar, objects are often specular or rotationally symmetric, and typical per-frame jitter (1–3 mm / 1–2°) is sub-pixel at HOI4D viewing distances. In these null spaces of the rendering loss the parameterization suppresses jitter by PRIOR, not by pixel evidence — philosophically the same as a filter — so the central ablation (joint pixel optimization vs baseline+SmoothNet/spline post-fit) may show a small or zero accuracy delta, leaving only smoothness gains that a spline post-fit also achieves. The whole paper stands or falls on this one ablation and it has a realistic chance of coming out flat.

Contact-segmentation cascade: SAM2 mask adjacency + proximity is a weak grasp detector (hovering ≠ grasping; occlusion merges masks; regrasps split poorly). A wrong contact segment imposes rigid attachment on a free object (or vice versa), producing large correlated errors — a strictly worse failure mode than the baselines' independent per-frame noise, and one reviewers will probe with regrasp/handover clips.

Novelty is assembly-level and the field is closing fast: BIGS (CVPR'25) owns rigged-GS-for-HOI, Get a Grip (ECCV'24) owns hand-relative grasp factorization, SplineGS/HOIGS own splines-in-GS, GraG already markets jitter suppression, and CARI4D (CVPR'26, NVIDIA) claims category-agnostic METRIC-SCALE temporally consistent 4D HOI via render-and-compare + contact reasoning. The remaining delta — composing these inside one GS objective — reads as 'known ingredients, new glue' unless gains are large; that is the canonical CVPR borderline-reject profile.

The evaluation-protocol contribution is also eroding: acceleration-error metrics (Acc-h/Acc-o vs GT) already appear in 2026 4D-HOI papers (e.g., THO spatial-temporal transformer lineage, CARI4D), and accel error has been standard in human motion since VIBE. 'First temporal-stability benchmark for GS-based HOI with GT depth' survives, but that is a thin qualifier, not a headline claim.

Temporal metrics are gameable by construction and reviewers know it: a spline parameterization trivially wins jitter/accel/scale-constancy while risking lag and oversmoothing of true fast motion (regrasps, impacts). Worse, measuring mm/s² acceleration error requires per-frame GT object pose far more accurate than HOI4D's (partly interpolated, annotator-noisy) annotations provide — the evaluation may be measuring GT noise. Mocap-grade alternatives (ARCTIC, DexYCB, HO3D) have templates and template-based SOTA that would beat a SAM-3D-mesh method on raw accuracy, an unflattering comparison the paper cannot avoid being asked for.

Baseline reproduction risk: GHOST and GraG are preprints with unverified code availability; BIGS was evaluated under a different protocol. If these cannot be run fairly on the HOI4D GT-depth harness in world-frame metric terms, the comparison table degrades to the user's own 4 pipelines plus filters, weakening the SOTA claim.

Headline motivation numbers are vulnerable: the −29% to −81% depth and +33–43% size errors quoted for baselines come from methods NOT given the depth signal this method uses. The mandatory fairness ablation (baseline + same depth term + global scale correction + post-filter) may close most of the motivating gap before the proposed machinery even enters.

Scooping window: submission would target CVPR 2027 (Nov 2026 deadline); given 4+ GS-HOI entries in the 2026 preprint wave alone, the probability that a contact-factorized or continuous-time HOI-GS paper appears before then is substantial, and the branch has no second line of defense if the parameterization claim is taken.
unsound_assumptions: 'Jitter cannot exist unless it improves photometric fit in every frame' — false as stated: jitter lives in the photometric null space (occluded, textureless, symmetric, motion-blurred regions), which is precisely where per-frame methods jitter most; there the parameterization acts as a prior indistinguishable in kind from a filter.

Basin-of-convergence assumption (~15°/~3 cm from per-frame init) is contradicted by the branch's OWN harness evidence of −29% to −81% absolute depth error and +33–43% size error in the initializing pipelines; coarse-to-fine + DINOv2 widening the basin that far is asserted, not evidenced.

Grasp rigidity within mask-adjacency-detected segments: adjacency is not contact, and in-hand rotation/rolling manipulation (common in HOI4D categories like scissors, kettle pouring) violates the single-G_k-plus-slow-drift model in ways soft blending only papers over.

Time-invariant object appearance with per-frame GLOBAL affine exposure: the hand casts strong spatially-varying moving shadows and inter-reflections on the object during manipulation; a global affine cannot absorb this, injecting structured photometric error exactly at the contact region the method cares most about.
HOI4D GT object-pose annotations are accurate and temporally dense enough to score acceleration error in mm/s² — unverified and likely false for second-derivative metrics.
BIGS/GHOST/GraG code runs on HOI4D for direct world-frame metric comparison — GHOST and GraG are preprints; code release and protocol compatibility are unverified.

That matching do-as-i-do's 1–4 GPU-h budget is acceptable to reviewers when CARI4D and feed-forward competitors (THO at 31.5 FPS) are simultaneously claiming comparable temporal consistency at orders-of-magnitude lower cost — 'offline is fine' is a 2024 assumption applied to a 2027 reviewing climate.

feasibility.data: MODERATE. HOI4D with GT depth exists and the team's harness already runs on it, but ~20–30 clips is a small benchmark for cross-category claims, GT pose annotation quality is likely insufficient for second-derivative (acceleration) metrics, and the mocap-grade alternatives (ARCTIC/DexYCB/HO3D) come with object templates that both undercut the 'unknown object' story and invite unflattering comparison to template-based SOTA. In-the-wild results will be qualitative only.
feasibility.compute: GOOD. 1–4 GPU-h/clip × ~30 clips × (method + ~6 ablations + 7–9 baselines/filter variants) ≈ 500–1500 GPU-h — comfortably within a rented multi-GPU budget over 2–3 months. The differentiable pipeline (two rigged Gaussian sets, spline chain rule, segment blending) is heavy engineering but all components have public reference implementations (GART, gsplat, Theseus/LieTorch splines).
feasibility.evaluation: MEDIUM-RISK, and it is where the paper lives or dies. Strengths: the harness exists, and the proposed filter-ablation (baseline + OneEuro/SmoothNet/spline post-fit) is the right experiment. Risks: (1) that very ablation may show the parameterization adds little over spline post-fitting on accuracy, since temporal metrics favor splines by construction; (2) fairness demands giving baselines the same depth signal, which may erase the motivating scale/depth gaps; (3) GHOST/GraG reproduction is unverified; (4) accel-error metrics are already appearing in 2026 4D-HOI papers, so the protocol is not cleanly first. A 2–3 clip pilot of the full Stage A→C loop versus per-frame+SmoothNet is cheap (~1 week) and would settle the make-or-break question before committing.

pressure.verdict_reason: The technical core is genuinely specified (not vague) and the contact-factorized continuous-time parameterization is a real, unclaimed mechanism — but it is a narrow, assembly-level delta in one of the most crowded lineages in 3D vision (BIGS, GHOST, GraG, HOIGS, Interaction-Aware 4DGS, and now CARI4D at CVPR'26 claiming metric-scale temporally-consistent category-agnostic 4D HOI), and the entire paper rests on one ablation — joint pixel-level spline optimization decisively beating per-frame baselines + spline/SmoothNet post-filtering on ACCURACY, not just on smoothness metrics that splines win by construction — which has a realistic chance of coming out flat because the photometric signal is weakest (occlusion, texturelessness, sub-pixel jitter) exactly where jitter is worst, and because the factorization imports wrist-tracking error into the object trajectory. Pursue ONLY after a 1-week, 2–3-clip pilot: if the full parameterization beats per-frame+SmoothNet by a clear margin on both ADD/depth accuracy AND stability with fair depth access for baselines, the paper has a defensible CVPR core; if the margin is small, drop or pivot the contribution to the GT-depth temporal-stability benchmark/harness itself (a dataset/eval paper), because the mechanism alone will not survive review.

branch.title: Contact-aware compositional 4DGS: hand + object + static-background Gaussians jointly optimized with contact and non-penetration constraints defined in Gaussian space
branch.angle: Interaction physics as the differentiator: extend b2's compositional scene with (i) a static background Gaussian layer that anchors camera pose and metric scale, and (ii) contact energies coupling the hand and object Gaussian sets — attraction of contact-labeled hand Gaussians to the object surface during grasp phases, SDF-style non-penetration, and shared-motion constraints while in contact (object velocity tied to contacting-hand velocity, detected via TAPIR/CHOIR-style contact inference).
branch.core_hypothesis: Relative hand-object jitter (floating/penetration flicker) is the perceptually and metrically dominant failure mode, and photometric losses alone under-constrain the interaction; contact coupling in the joint GS optimization removes it, directly improving the contact and relative-depth metrics in the HOI4D harness where all 4 baselines fail.
branch.why_distinct: The novelty claim is contact-in-the-GS-loop plus background-anchored scale — a constraint structure absent from hand-avatar GS, MANUS (multi-view, known setup), and generic dynamic-GS works. b2 could exist without any contact term; b3 is specifically about the hand-object coupling and full-scene composition.

clarification.problem_statement: Given a single monocular RGB video (moving/egocentric camera) of a hand manipulating an unknown rigid object, recover a metrically scaled 4D reconstruction — MANO hand trajectory, model-free object shape with its SE(3) trajectory, and camera path — that is simultaneously per-frame accurate AND temporally/physically consistent: no hand-object floating, no interpenetration flicker, no relative-depth or scale drift. All four pipelines evaluated on our HOI4D GT-depth harness (render_and_compare, do-as-i-do, ForeHOI, HORT) fail this: monocular methods mis-scale the object by +33–43% and misplace its depth by −29% to −81% (kettle clip C12/N15), and every method exhibits relative hand-object jitter that required ad-hoc temporal-smoothing patches — because they estimate frames (nearly) independently and couple hand and object only through per-frame heuristics, so monocular evidence never constrains the interaction itself. The problem is to reformulate 4D HOI reconstruction as one full-clip test-time optimization in which temporal smoothness and contact physics are structural properties of the parametrization, not post-hoc filters — within the multi-hour per-clip budget that existing pipelines (do-as-i-do: ~3 h per 5 s clip) already spend.
clarification.technical_core: A three-layer compositional 4D Gaussian scene rendered through one differentiable rasterizer with alpha compositing, optimized jointly over the whole clip. (1) BACKGROUND layer: static world-frame 3DGS initialized from hand/object-masked metric SLAM (DROID/MASt3R-SLAM + MoGe/UniDepth metric depth), with per-frame camera SE(3) refined SplaTAM-style; static-by-parametrization, it pins the camera trajectory and the metric scale gauge so hand-object relative-depth errors become photometrically visible misalignments (this is exactly the anchor that made render_and_compare GT-exact when GT depth was injected — here recovered, not given). (2) HAND layer: Gaussians rigged to MANO (barycentric face attachment + LBS); free parameters are shape beta, per-Gaussian appearance/opacity/scale, and a continuous-time pose trajectory — wrist SE(3) and PCA-articulation as cubic B-splines in se(3) with knots every ~0.2 s, so the trajectory is band-limited and jitter is unrepresentable. (3) OBJECT layer: canonical model-free Gaussians (initialized from SAM-3D/HORT lifted by clip-wide fusion, which also fills hand-occluded regions) plus a rigid SE(3) spline trajectory. CONTACT COUPLING, the differentiator, is one reparametrization plus two Gaussian-space energies, gated by an inferred contact posterior: (a) phase detection — CHOIR dense hand-contact fields (already in the render_and_compare backend) fused with a track test (TAPIR/CoTracker tracks on the object mask are marked in-contact when their motion is rigidly explained by wrist motion over a window), segmenting the clip into free/approach/grasp/release; (b) grasp-phase reparametrization — during each grasp phase p the object trajectory becomes T_o(t) = T_wrist(t) ∘ G_p ∘ ΔT(t) with G_p one constant grasp transform and ΔT(t) an identity-regularized slack spline, structurally deleting the relative-pose DOF that produce floating/flicker while still permitting evidence-driven in-hand slip; (c) attraction — contact-labeled hand Gaussians x_i are pulled to the object iso-surface using the object Gaussian mixture density F_o(x)=Σ_k o_k N(x; μ_k, Σ_k) as a soft SDF: E_att = Σ_i (F_o(x_i) − τ)²; (d) non-penetration, symmetric — E_pen = Σ_k ReLU(−sdf_MANO(μ_k^obj))² using the exact differentiable point-to-mesh SDF of the posed watertight MANO, plus Σ_{i∉contact} ReLU(F_o(x_i) − τ)² for hand Gaussians. Full objective: photometric L1 + D-SSIM on the composite render, per-layer SAM2/SAM3 video-mask supervision (point-prompt protocol already validated on the harness), rendered-depth vs. metric mono-depth consistency, long-range 2D track reprojection on hand and object Gaussians (disambiguates low-texture skin/plastic), E_att + E_pen, and spline acceleration priors. Optimization schedule fitting the multi-hour budget: Stage A masked background SLAM + camera; Stage B per-frame initialization (WiLoR/HaMeR hand, HORT/SAM-3D object) fit by splines; Stage C joint photometric refinement without contact; Stage D 2–3 EM rounds — E-step re-estimate contact posteriors/phase boundaries from current geometry and tracks, M-step re-optimize with (b)–(d) — making contact inference self-correcting rather than trusted upfront. Evaluation reuses the existing HOI4D GT-depth harness and the four adapted baselines in the common scene format: current size/depth-error metrics plus new interaction metrics (relative hand-object pose acceleration RMS, penetration depth/volume rate, contact-persistence IoU against contact derived from HOI4D GT hand+object poses) and per-frame chamfer/MPJPE to demonstrate no accuracy trade-off; ablations peel off contact terms (recovering the b2 baseline), background layer, splines, and grasp reparametrization to attribute the gains.
clarification.novelty_claim: The first monocular in-the-wild 4D hand-object reconstruction that puts interaction physics inside the splatting optimization itself — a hand-rigged + model-free-object + static-background compositional Gaussian scene whose object trajectory is reparametrized through per-grasp constant grasp transforms and regularized by Gaussian-density contact-attraction and non-penetration energies, so contact consistency and temporal smoothness hold by construction — a constraint structure absent from HOLD (per-frame implicit-SDF poses, no contact/background/scale anchor), MANUS (multi-view rig, known setup), hand-avatar GS (hand-only), and HUGS-style human-scene composition (no object, no contact).
clarification.target_venue: CVPR (primary: reconstruction-system contribution with a rigorous quantitative harness and 4 reproduced baselines; CoRL as fallback if repitched as a demonstration-data engine for manipulation policy learning)
key_assumptions: The manipulated object is rigid (HOI4D-style manipulation); articulated/deformable objects are out of scope or a stated extension.

Contact-phase detection (CHOIR contact fields + rigid-track-correlation) is precise enough that grasp phases are correctly segmented; false-positive contact is the main risk, mitigated by soft posteriors, the identity-regularized slack spline, and EM re-estimation rather than hard upfront trust.

There is enough camera motion and background texture/parallax for masked metric SLAM to anchor scale and camera (true for egocentric HOI4D; degrades on static-tripod textureless scenes, where scale falls back to metric mono-depth priors).

Per-frame initializations (WiLoR/HaMeR hand, SAM-3D/HORT object, SAM2/SAM3 point-prompt masks — all already wired in the repo) land within the basin of convergence of the joint photometric refinement.
Accumulating object observations across the clip provides enough angular coverage to fuse a usable canonical Gaussian shape despite persistent hand occlusion.

Relative hand-object jitter, floating, and penetration flicker are the dominant residual failure mode (supported by the harness: +33-43% size / -29-81% depth errors for monocular baselines, plus the documented temporal-smoothing and scale-fix patches), and reviewers will accept new temporal/contact metrics alongside standard per-frame ones.

A multi-hour offline per-clip budget is acceptable to the community for this problem (precedent: do-as-i-do already spends ~3 h on a 5 s clip; HOLD-style per-clip optimization is an accepted paradigm).

Photometric splatting loss is informative on low-texture skin and objects once combined with mask and long-track losses; motion blur and specularities are handled by robust losses rather than breaking convergence.

GT contact for the contact-persistence metric can be derived from HOI4D's GT hand and object pose annotations (proximity thresholding), since HOI4D ships GT depth and poses but not explicit contact labels.

novelty.delta: Not already done as a whole, but the headline claim needs rewriting. Every individual ingredient is now published: contact-as-coupling-signal joint optimization on monocular video (CHOIR '26, HOLD '24), grasp-aware contact alignment inside a monocular GS pipeline (GHOST '26), phase-structured GS optimization for manipulation (Clay-to-Stone CVPR'26 Highlight), MANO-rigged + model-free-object Gaussians (BIGS CVPR'25), background/hand/object compositional egocentric GS (DP-DeGauss '26, Interaction-Aware 4DGS '25), SLAM+metric-depth world anchoring (HaWoR CVPR'25), and simulator-grade interaction physics with wrist-welded object motion and spline trajectories (Grasp-and-Lift '26). The surviving delta is the specific constraint STRUCTURE and the metrology: (1) a metric SLAM-anchored static-background GS layer that turns hand-object relative-depth/scale errors into photometric residuals — absent from all HOI-GS works, which drop the background and leave scale unanchored (the +33-43% size errors the harness documents); (2) grasp-phase kinematic reparametrization T_o=T_wrist∘G_p∘ΔT plus band-limited se(3) splines, making jitter and floating unrepresentable by construction rather than penalized (GHOST/CHOIR/HOLD all use soft losses or one-shot alignment; Clay-to-Stone's phases target articulation rigidity, not hand-object coupling); (3) Gaussian-mixture-density attraction + posed-MANO-SDF non-penetration as energies inside the whole-clip splatting objective with EM contact re-estimation; and (4) an evaluation contribution: GT-depth harness with 4 reproduced baselines and new relative-jitter/penetration/contact-persistence metrics. To be defensible at CVPR the paper must position against and empirically beat GHOST, CHOIR, and BIGS (not just HOLD/MANUS), and the claim should be 'structural contact coupling + background-anchored metric scale in compositional 4DGS', not 'first contact in splatting'.
novelty.crowdedness_reason: Monocular hand-object reconstruction with Gaussian splatting has become one of the hottest micro-niches of 2025-2026: at least eight directly overlapping papers appeared in the last ~14 months (BIGS CVPR'25, Interaction-Aware 4DGS 11/25, Grasp-and-Lift 1/26, AGILE 2/26, GHOST 3/26, GraG 4/26, DP-DeGauss 4/26, CHOIR 5/26, Clay-to-Stone CVPR'26 Highlight), and two of them (GHOST, CHOIR) already claim contact-aware/physically-consistent monocular HOI. The exact intersection proposed (background-anchored metric scale + structural grasp coupling + contact energies in one 4DGS optimization) is still unclaimed, so it is 'crowded' rather than 'saturated' — but the window is closing fast and concurrent-work collisions by a CVPR 2027 deadline are likely.

failure_modes: Concurrent-work collision is near-certain, not hypothetical: 8+ monocular HOI-GS papers in 14 months, two of which (GHOST 3/26, CHOIR 5/26) already claim contact-aware/physically-consistent monocular HOI, and Clay-to-Stone (CVPR'26 Highlight) already published phase-structured GS optimization for manipulation. By a Nov 2026 CVPR'27 deadline the surviving delta ('constraint structure + background scale anchor') will read to reviewers as a recombination of published ingredients, and 1-2 more collisions in the interim are likely.

The grasp weld T_o = T_wrist ∘ G_p ∘ ΔT structurally propagates hand errors into the object — the exact bug this team already diagnosed in its own harness: do-as-i-do's hand-anchored depth inherited HaWoR's +28% hand-depth error until they replaced it with a GT anchor. Monocular wrist SE(3) (WiLoR/HaMeR) is depth-ambiguous and jittery; welding the object to it trades hand-object relative jitter for correlated absolute error, and the joint optimization must fix the hand and object simultaneously for the weld to help — a circular dependency the proposal never resolves.

EM contact-phase estimation over discrete grasp boundaries inside a nonconvex photometric landscape is fragile: a mis-detected grasp onset welds the object to the wrist during approach (object drags/teleports), and once the M-step has satisfied the weld photometrically, the E-step has little gradient signal to undo it. Soft posteriors + slack splines mitigate but also reintroduce the very relative-pose DOF the reparametrization claims to delete — the method's headline ('jitter unrepresentable by construction') and its escape hatch (identity-regularized ΔT(t) slack) are in direct tension.

The claim that a background GS layer makes relative-depth errors 'photometrically visible' is optically weak: depth errors along the optical axis are precisely what photometric losses are least sensitive to under the small parallax of a 5 s handheld clip. The real depth signal is the rendered-depth vs. metric-monodepth loss — which any baseline could bolt on — so the ablation must disentangle 'contact structure' gains from plain depth supervision, and reviewers will suspect the latter explains most of the scale/depth improvement.

Self-serving evaluation circularity: the proposed new metrics (relative pose acceleration RMS, penetration rate, contact-persistence IoU) are exactly the quantities the method's constraints enforce by construction. A trivially wrist-welded object scores perfectly on all three while being geometrically wrong. Unless the method also wins (not just ties) on independent per-frame chamfer/MPJPE/ADD, an AC will read the metric suite as designed for the method.

The Gaussian-mixture density F_o(x) as a soft SDF has a known degenerate solution: the optimizer can satisfy E_att and E_pen by shrinking opacities/scales of Gaussians near the contact region instead of moving geometry, since o_k, Σ_k are co-optimized with μ_k. This requires detach schedules and per-term LR surgery — exactly the fragile-hyperparameter territory that kills reproducibility and rebuttals.

The motivating evidence is n=1: the entire quantitative case (+33-43% size, −29 to −81% depth) comes from ONE 5-second kettle clip (compare/hoi4d/depth_eval.md), and the 'jitter is dominant' claim from one commit-level flicker fix — which, tellingly, a cheap temporal depth-smoothing patch already fixed. If a 10-line smoothing filter removes the perceptual artifact, demonstrating that hours of structural contact machinery buys a visible margin over 'baseline + smoothing + monodepth loss' is a genuinely hard experimental bar.

Baseline reproduction gap: to be defensible the paper must beat GHOST, CHOIR, and BIGS, but GHOST and CHOIR are 2026 arXiv works with uncertain code release; comparing only against HOLD/HORT/ForeHOI (what the harness has) invites a one-line rejection for missing the closest published baselines, and re-implementing either is a multi-month project by itself.

Benchmark scale-up cost: a credible CVPR paper needs ~30-50 HOI4D clips plus HO3D/ARCTIC or in-the-wild results for comparability; at multi-hour whole-clip optimization × (method + 5 ablations) this is hundreds of GPU-hours of turnaround per experimental iteration, which slows the debug loop of an already fragile multi-stage system (masked SLAM → per-frame init → joint photometric → EM contact) where any stage failing sinks the clip.

Paradigm-timing risk: the field is visibly moving feed-forward (HORT ~1 min, GraG advertises 6.4x faster tracking); a multi-hour per-clip test-time optimization pitched at CVPR 2027 continues a 2024 paradigm (HOLD) and will draw 'expensive per-scene optimization, limited practical relevance' reviews unless the accuracy gap over fast methods is dramatic.
unsound_assumptions: 'Relative hand-object jitter is the perceptually and metrically dominant failure mode' — the harness actually documents SCALE and DEPTH errors as dominant (addressed by the background/depth anchor, not by contact coupling); the jitter evidence is one flicker anecdote already fixed by trivial temporal smoothing, so the differentiating machinery targets the weaker-evidenced failure.

'Per-frame initializations land within the basin of convergence of joint photometric refinement' — contradicted by the harness itself: HORT places the object at −81% depth; nothing photometric recovers from that, so convergence actually rests on the depth/track losses being strong enough to move the object ~0.7 m, which is asserted, not shown.

'Background GS layer turns relative-depth/scale errors into photometric residuals' — under 5 s of handheld parallax, along-axis depth errors are nearly photometrically invisible; the anchor that was 'GT-exact' in render_and_compare used injected GT depth, and replacing GT depth with SLAM+monodepth (5-15% metric error typical) does not license extrapolating that exactness.

'Reviewers will accept new temporal/contact metrics alongside standard ones' — risky when the new metrics are optimized by construction; acceptance hinges on winning independent metrics, which the proposal only promises to 'not trade off'.

'GT contact can be derived from HOI4D GT poses by proximity thresholding' — HOI4D object-pose annotations have documented noise at the centimeter level, comparable to the contact threshold itself, so the contact-persistence GT is itself uncertain in exactly the regime being measured.

'Soft posteriors + EM make contact inference self-correcting' — EM over discrete phase boundaries with a photometric M-step has no guarantee of escaping a wrong initial segmentation; CHOIR's dynamically-updated contact constraints already occupy this idea, so it is both fragile and non-novel.

'Clip-wide fusion provides enough angular coverage for canonical object shape' — HOI4D manipulations are short and one-sided; the object back face is often never observed, forcing a diffusion/SDS completion prior (as BIGS needed), which the technical core omits.

feasibility.data: Good raw availability, thin current state. HOI4D (GT depth + poses) is in hand and partially wired, SAM2/SAM3 mask protocol validated, four baselines adapted — but the harness today is ONE kettle clip (compare/hoi4d/depth_eval.md). Scaling to 30-50 rigid-object clips across categories plus an external benchmark (HO3D/ARCTIC for comparability with GHOST/BIGS numbers) is mandatory and is weeks of curation; GT contact labels must be synthesized from noisy pose annotations. Rigid-only scope excludes several HOI4D categories.
feasibility.compute: Acceptable but painful. Single-GPU per clip is fine; the problem is iteration velocity: whole-clip 4DGS + per-iteration posed-MANO SDF + spline optimization + 2-3 EM rounds plausibly lands at 2-6 h/clip, and a full result table (method + 5 ablations + 4 baselines × ~30-50 clips) is 500-1500 GPU-hours per experimental sweep. On rented GPUs this is affordable in money but expensive in debug-loop latency for a system with 4 sequential fragile stages.
feasibility.evaluation: The weakest leg. (1) Closest baselines GHOST/CHOIR/BIGS likely lack usable code; without beating them head-to-head the novelty delta collapses to unverifiable prose. (2) The three new interaction metrics are enforced by the method's own constraints — circular unless per-frame chamfer/MPJPE/ADD also improve, which the mechanism gives no strong reason to expect. (3) The most damaging ablation ('baseline + temporal smoothing + monodepth loss', i.e., the cheap fixes already applied in this repo) is exactly the one reviewers will demand and the one the structural machinery may fail to clearly beat.

pressure.verdict_reason: As specified, this is a 2026-vintage recombination entering the single most crowded micro-niche in the area, with its headline mechanism (contact coupling) targeting the weaker-evidenced failure mode (n=1 flicker anecdote already fixed by cheap smoothing) while its stronger-evidenced problem (metric scale/depth, +33-43%/−81% on one clip) is addressed by an ingredient (SLAM+monodepth background anchoring) that is closest to a bolt-on depth loss any baseline could adopt. It escapes 'drop' only because two assets are real and rare: a GT-depth harness with four reproduced baselines (currently n=1 clip — must become n≈40 before anything else), and the genuinely unclaimed metric-background-anchored composition. Pursue only under a hard repositioning: lead with the benchmark/metrology contribution plus background-anchored metric scale, demote contact energies to one ablated component, budget for reproducing or numerically matching GHOST/CHOIR/BIGS, and pre-register the killer ablation (baseline + smoothing + monodepth loss) — if that ablation closes most of the gap in a 2-3 week pilot on ~10 clips, drop the branch.

digest.kill_test: 2-3 week pilot on ~10 HOI4D clips: best baseline + temporal smoothing + monodepth loss vs. full contact-coupled system. Go if structural coupling clearly wins scale/depth AND chamfer; kill if the cheap bolt-on closes most of the gap.
